input.title: Store carts in Postgres or Redis instead of the 4 KB cookie?
input.body:
**Summary:** The session cookie is capped at 4 KB, so long carts get truncated. Either option moves the cart server-side and leaves only an opaque cart ID in the cookie.

**Example:** A shopper adds 40 line items. The cookie can't hold them, so the cart silently loses items at checkout.

**Postgres:** Durable and queryable, so you can run abandoned-cart reports and keep carts across restarts. It adds a write per cart change and needs a cleanup job for old carts. Usually fewer moving parts if you already run it.

**Redis:** Fast, with built-in TTLs that expire abandoned carts automatically. Carts are lost on eviction or a misconfigured persistence setting unless you enable AOF/RDB. It adds infrastructure if you don't already run it.

**My pick:** Postgres. A lost cart is lost revenue, and carts are business data you may want to query. Choose Redis instead if you already run it and cart writes are hot enough that DB load matters.

**Not checked:** I didn't read the codebase, so I don't know which of these you already run.

content.text:
A1 [open] decision: Store carts in Postgres or Redis instead of the 4 KB cookie?
actions: a1 resolve "Postgres (recommended)", a2 resolve "Redis"
